title: Decide the counterexample tag: column, widened shape, or documented floor
description: The resolution side of the tag decision closed on 2026-10-07 as the resolves_named column; the counterexample side is open. Measured 2026-10-06: 74 of 372 families use counterexample language in title or abstract and only 44 carry the counterexample tag; of the 31 untagged flags, 30 are genuine in kind and the false positive is 348, matched through 'nonnegatively'. Three options: (a) add a counterex_named column and keep the shape at 44; (b) widen the shape to 74; (c) leave 44 as a documented floor with no code change. Option (b) moves families between T0 buckets, because triage_t0.py assigns buckets by first match and counterexample is first in its chain. If a column is chosen, follow the generated-index-column-change skill: measure the yield first, read every new flag, prove additivity by diffing notes/catalog.tsv column by column, then sweep every doc that names the schema (notes/README.md, notes/t0-triage.md, the proof-triage skill).

title: Roll the notes/ reading records into one findings index
description:
Reading findings are scattered by method, not by family: notes/t0-triage.md (137 families), notes/resolution-tag.md (233), notes/conditional.md (9 flagged, 5 real), notes/verification-dirs.md (30 dirs). Answering "what did we conclude about family NNN" means reading four documents and matching by hand.

Build notes/findings.tsv, one row per family: fam, discipline, claim shape, tier, evidence columns from the ledger, the reading verdict where one exists, and which notes/ document the verdict comes from. Generated by a stdlib script over notes/*.md plus notes/catalog.tsv, byte-identical on rerun, reconciling 372 rows. Findings stay in the tracked notes/ files; the index is a join, not a new record of record.

title: Index the 722 manuscript sources into notes/sources.tsv
description:
Write notes/scripts/build_sources.py, stdlib only, no Lean, no PDF parsing: for each of the 722 preprints/<dir>/, emit family dir, manuscript PDF path, main tex path, tex file count, .bib count, section count, \begin{proof} count, theorem-like environment count, abstract present, total tex bytes.

Main-file resolution rule, measured 2026-10-07: 717 of 722 directories contain exactly one file with \documentclass and 5 contain two or three; the documentclass file is main.tex in 495, paper.tex in 210, and one of 21 other names in the remaining 17 (preamble.tex 8, manuscript.tex 3, common.tex 2, and 4 singletons). Prefer main.tex/paper.tex, fall back to the \documentclass file, and flag multi-root directories rather than guessing.

Acceptance: 722 rows; running the script twice yields byte-identical output; the family set and manuscript PDF paths reconcile with notes/catalog.tsv with zero differences.

title: Mine the manuscript LaTeX sources under preprints/
description:
preprints/ is not PDF-only. Measured 2026-10-07: all 722 family directories ship the manuscript as LaTeX source — 7,729 .tex files, 501 .bib, 128 MB of source, 177 KB average per family. Every directory has exactly one PDF at its root (the manuscript, named article.pdf in most, paper.pdf/main.pdf/manuscript.pdf/final.pdf in the rest) plus a build/ tree holding the source and a README.md citation stub.

Content signals already present in the sources, counted corpus-wide: 20,449 \begin{proof}, 21,317 theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary/claim/conjecture environments, and \begin{abstract} in 722 of 722 directories. The ledger uses none of this: its abstracts come from overview.tex, and its claim shapes are derived from those abstracts alone.

Children add a source index, cross-check the two abstracts, test proof density as a ledger signal, build the citation graph, and inventory numbered results. All of it is static reading over text files: never run lake, lean, or comparator, and quote counts only from a fresh build_catalog.py report.

title: Test proof density as a ledger signal before adding it as a column
description:
Corpus totals measured 2026-10-07: 20,449 \begin{proof} and 21,317 theorem-like environments over 722 manuscripts. Compute proofs-per-family and statements-per-family from the source index, then test whether the distribution separates the tiers (T3 127 / T2 108 / T1 0 / T0 137 per the generator report) or the claim shapes.

Follow the conditional-tag discipline: a new signal is only quotable after it discriminates. If proof density separates nothing, record the null result in notes/ and do not add the column; if it does, add it via the generated-index-column-change procedure, which keeps broad rules out of first-match chains and proves additivity by diffing the ledger column by column.

title: Cross-check the 722 manuscript abstracts against the overview.tex abstracts
description:
Every manuscript ships its own \begin{abstract} (722 of 722 directories) while the ledger's claim-shape tags are keyword rules over the abstract text in overview.tex. Compare the two texts per family: identical, abridged, or materially different. Report the counts and quote the largest divergences.

Why it matters: if the overview.tex abstract is a summary rather than the manuscript abstract, the shapes tags are keyed to a paraphrase, and the conditional-tag lesson (9 flagged, 5 real) says a tag built on thin text overstates. Record findings in notes/abstracts.md, one entry per divergent family, stating which text the tag should read.

title: Build the shared-bibliography graph from the 501 .bib files
description:
501 .bib files sit in the preprint build trees. Parse entry keys and titles, then report which manuscripts share references: pairs and clusters with a shared citation, and the most-cited entries corpus-wide. Shared references are a categorization signal the ledger does not have — the disciplines in overview.tex are the release's own grouping, and a citation cluster crossing discipline boundaries is evidence that a grouping is arbitrary.

Record findings in notes/citations.md: cluster membership, the discipline crossings, and the top cited entries with counts. Do not infer a family's result from its bibliography.

title: Inventory the numbered results named in the manuscript sources
description:
The resolves_named column (233 families, union 238 per the generator report) is derived from titles in overview.tex. The sources carry the statements themselves: 21,317 theorem-like environments. Extract the numbered theorem/theorem-name statements per family, keeping only the headline result statements, and compare that inventory against resolves_named.

Report the families where the source names a result the title-derived column misses, and the families where the title names something the source does not state. This is the check that turns resolves_named from a title heuristic into an evidence-backed column; record it in notes/ and keep it a column, not a shape.
